title: Every living thing from water
hookLine: We made every living thing from water (21:30)
tomorrow: Dawud and Sulayman judge a field

cards: Turn on a tap and fill a glass. It takes three seconds, and where water is cheap it costs almost nothing, so it's easy to forget what's in your hand. Leave a plant without it and it droops.
Go without it yourself and you won't last long. Surah twenty-one, Al-Anbiya, the Prophets, stops in the middle of a long argument about God on a short line about what's in that glass.

teach.b: Al-Anbiya is named for the prophets; it walks through many of them, Ibrahim, Musa, Dawud, Sulayman, Ayyub, Yunus and more. But first, it points at the world.
Verse thirty, in Pickthall's words: "Have not those who disbelieve known that the heavens and the earth were of one piece, then We parted them, and we made every living thing of water?"
And it ends: will they not then believe? A question, then a sign, then another question. It isn't a lecture.
It asks people to look at what's already in front of them.

Some modern readers connect the verse with what biology says about water and life; other scholars caution against reading the Qur'an as a science textbook, since its purpose here is a sign that leads to faith.
Both are said within the tradition.

teach.h: LIFE FROM WATER, WATER FROM GOD.
teach.b: What the verse plainly says: life comes from water, and water comes from God. A verse in An-Nur says God created every animal from water: some go on their bellies, some on two legs, some on four.
In Muslim practice, water comes before prayer: wudu, washing the hands, mouth, nose, face and arms, wiping the head, washing the feet.
And a hadith in Abu Dawud says Muslims are partners in three things: water, pasture and fire.
Water isn't meant to be hoarded. So one line holds three things at once: a sign of the Creator, a gift to all living things, and a trust to be shared. The glass from the tap is all three.

how: Muslims make wudu with water before prayer, and some follow the Prophet's practice of saying bismillah and drinking in three sips while seated; 21:30 is often cited when teaching care for water.

games.q: you've filled a glass at the tap. according to 21:30, what is it a sign of?
o: the Creator who made every living thing from water.
games.why: the verse points to water as a sign that leads to faith: life from water, and water from God.

practice: Pour a glass of water, or picture one, and think back along its road: rain, a river or a reservoir, pipes, the tap.
Muslim custom, drawn from hadith, is to say bismillah before drinking and to drink in three sips, sitting down; if you'd like, try that. Then sit with the empty glass, and let the thanks be wordless.
